title: Geography Masters
intro: Hidden capitals, mighty rivers, tricky borders and flags in words. Only true map lovers need apply.

questions.prompt: What is the capital of Kazakhstan?
questions.explanation: Astana replaced Almaty as capital in 1997. Almaty is still Kazakhstan's largest city.

questions.prompt: What is the capital of Bhutan?
questions.explanation: Thimphu sits high in a Himalayan valley. Kathmandu is the capital of neighbouring Nepal.

questions.prompt: What is the capital of Myanmar?
questions.explanation: Myanmar moved its capital from Yangon to the purpose-built city of Naypyidaw in 2005 and 2006.

questions.prompt: What is the capital of Morocco?
questions.explanation: Rabat, on the Atlantic coast, is the capital, although Casablanca is the largest city.

questions.prompt: What is the official capital of Tanzania?
questions.explanation: Dodoma was named the capital in the 1970s, but Dar es Salaam remains the largest city and main port.

questions.prompt: Which city is the constitutional capital of Bolivia?
questions.explanation: Sucre is the constitutional capital and home of the supreme court, while La Paz is the seat of government.

questions.prompt: Which river forms much of the border between the United States and Mexico?
questions.explanation: The Rio Grande marks the border for about 2,000 km, from El Paso to the Gulf of Mexico. In Mexico it is called the Río Bravo.

questions.prompt: Into which body of water does the River Volga, Europe's longest river, flow?
questions.explanation: The Volga flows through western Russia and ends in a wide delta on the Caspian Sea.

questions.prompt: China borders 14 countries, a joint world record. Which other country shares that record?
questions.explanation: Both China and Russia have 14 neighbouring countries, more than any other nation.

questions.prompt: Which country is completely surrounded by South Africa?
questions.explanation: Lesotho is an enclave inside South Africa. All of its land lies above 1,000 metres, the highest low point of any country.

questions.prompt: Which country's flag has a green cedar tree in the centre, between two red horizontal stripes?
questions.explanation: The cedar of Lebanon has been a symbol of the land since ancient times and is mentioned many times in the Bible.

questions.prompt: Which country has the only national flag that is not a rectangle, shaped like two stacked pennants?
questions.explanation: Nepal's flag is two crimson triangles, one above the other, bordered in blue with a moon and sun.

questions.prompt: Which country's flag is a green field with a red disc set slightly towards the flagpole?
questions.explanation: On Bangladesh's flag, the green stands for the land and the red disc is often said to represent the sun rising over Bengal.

questions.prompt: Which is the deepest lake in the world?
questions.explanation: Lake Baikal in Siberia is over 1,600 metres deep and holds about a fifth of the world's unfrozen fresh surface water.

questions.prompt: Which is the longest continental mountain range in the world?
questions.explanation: The Andes run for about 7,000 km down the western side of South America.

questions.prompt: The Atacama, one of the driest deserts on Earth, lies mostly in which country?
questions.explanation: Parts of the Atacama can go years without measurable rain. Its clear, dry skies make it a favourite place for big telescopes.

questions.prompt: Which strait separates Europe from Africa at the western end of the Mediterranean?
questions.explanation: At its narrowest the Strait of Gibraltar is only about 13 km wide, between Spain and Morocco.

questions.prompt: Into which sea does the River Danube flow?
questions.explanation: The Danube rises in Germany's Black Forest and reaches the Black Sea in Romania, passing through or along ten countries.

questions.prompt: What is a long, narrow, steep-sided sea inlet carved out by a glacier called?
questions.explanation: Fjords form when glaciers carve deep valleys that the sea floods after the ice melts. Norway is famous for them.

questions.prompt: Which African river, the deepest known river in the world, crosses the equator twice?
questions.explanation: The Congo curves north across the equator and then back south. In places it is over 200 metres deep.

questions.prompt: Aconcagua, the highest mountain outside Asia, is in which country?
questions.explanation: Aconcagua rises to about 6,960 metres in the Andes of western Argentina, close to the Chilean border.

questions.prompt: Apart from Vatican City, which independent country lies entirely inside Italy?
questions.explanation: San Marino, on the slopes of Monte Titano, claims to be the world's oldest surviving republic.

questions.prompt: The city of Istanbul lies on two continents, Europe and Asia.
questions.explanation: The Bosporus strait runs through Istanbul, with part of the city in Europe and part in Asia.

questions.prompt: The shore of the Dead Sea is the lowest point on dry land on Earth.
questions.explanation: The Dead Sea's shore lies over 400 metres below sea level, and its water is so salty that people float easily.

questions.prompt: The equator passes through Brazil.
questions.explanation: The equator crosses northern Brazil near the mouth of the Amazon, so the country lies in both hemispheres.

questions.prompt: Switzerland has four national languages.
questions.explanation: Switzerland's national languages are German, French, Italian and Romansh.

questions.prompt: The Amazon River flows into the Pacific Ocean.
questions.explanation: The Amazon rises in the Andes but flows east across South America into the Atlantic Ocean.

questions.prompt: How many countries share a land border with Germany?
questions.explanation: Germany borders nine countries: Denmark, Poland, Czechia, Austria, Switzerland, France, Luxembourg, Belgium and the Netherlands.

questions.prompt: How many time zones does Russia span?
questions.explanation: Russia stretches across 11 time zones, from Kaliningrad in the west to Kamchatka in the far east.

questions.prompt: To the nearest whole degree, at what latitude north is the Tropic of Cancer?
questions.explanation: The Tropic of Cancer lies at about 23.4° north. It marks the most northerly place where the Sun can be directly overhead.
